text:
Dylan Larkin's season has been about everything except hockey. He asked Detroit for a trade in the summer, lost the captaincy in September, played ten games through boos at home, then told the Red Wings on Oct. 29 he would no longer play for them and was suspended. On Nov. 22 Detroit finally sent him to Montreal for Kirby Dach, prospect Michael Hage, goalie Sam Montembeault and a pile of picks, NHL.com reported. He debuted against the Kings on Monday with an assist in just under 20 minutes.

The hockey part looks better than the box score. In his 11 games his team took 56% of the expected goals at five on five, 6.5 points better than without him, but he's shooting 5.7% against a league norm of 13.5. That's the clearest bounce-back sign on his card: our range still has him scoring 20 to 37 goals by season's end.

In Montreal he's a second-line center behind Nick Suzuki, the job the Canadiens couldn't fill. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking says 67% of his shots last season came off the rush. Watch whether his new team lets him play that fast.
